sentences.text: Adult Psittacosaurus were obligate bipeds characterized by a high skull and a robust beak.
Individuals in this genus ranged from hatchlings under 13 cm long to adults nearly 2 meters long.
The best-known species, P. mongoliensis, could reach a length of 2 meters (6.5 feet).
Psittacosaurus is the most species-rich non-avian dinosaur genus, with up to 13 known species.
A 2022 study identified a specimen as a 6–7 year old subadult and found it preserves the first known umbilicus from a non-avian dinosaur.
The smallest known Psittacosaurus is a P. mongoliensis hatchling at the AMNH measuring only 11 to 13 centimetres long with a 2.4 cm skull.
Fossil evidence of a mixed-age herd of six individuals buried together provides the earliest known evidence of gregarious behavior in any ceratopsian dinosaur.
Henry Fairfield Osborn participated in the Third Asiatic Expedition of the American Museum of Natural History in 1922 to discover fossils in Mongolia.
Soviet expeditions discovered additional Psittacosaurus fossils in Mongolia between 1946 and 1949.
The species P. sinensis was discovered in the 1950s in the Aptian-Albian Qingshan Formation of Shandong Province, southeast of Beijing.
Researchers suggest Psittacosaurus jaws may have served a nutcracking function when the lower beak was retracted inside the upper beak.
Growth ring analysis estimated that basal ceratopsians like Psittacosaurus mongoliensis lived between 10 and 11 years.
Scientists hypothesize that heavy predation on juveniles led to R-selection, where the species produced many offspring to offset high mortality.
P. gobiensis is known from a skull and partial skeleton that includes gastroliths.
The encephalization quotient (EQ) of P. lujiatunensis is 0.31, which is significantly higher than that of genera like Triceratops.
A higher encephalization quotient correlates with more complex behavior, a trait seen in various dinosaurs and birds with EQs ranging from 0.36 to 2.98.
Psittacosaurus lujiatunensis had an encephalization quotient (EQ) of 0.31, which is significantly higher than that of Triceratops.
The genus Psittacosaurus includes seventeen referred species, though only nine to eleven are currently considered valid.
Psittacosaurus sinensis was distinguished by a shorter and wider snout and a smaller size of 675 mm.
Psittacosaurus is the type genus of the family Psittacosauridae, a name established by Osborn in 1923.
Psittacosaurus was once placed in its own family, Psittacosauridae, but is now considered the senior synonym of Hongshanosaurus.
Psittacosaurus lived between 125 and 105 million years ago.
Psittacosaurus mongoliensis fossils date to the Aptian to Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 125 to 100 million years ago.
While the age of the Jiufotang Formation in Liaoning is unknown, the neighboring Inner Mongolia province dates it to about 110 million years ago in the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous.
In 2010, Sereno tentatively regarded P. osborni as a synonym of P. mongoliensis due to the presence of other valid psittacosaur species in Inner Mongolia.
Paul Sereno questioned the validity of P. sattayaraki in 2000 due to its eroded, fragmentary nature and lack of characteristic Psittacosaurus features.
Studies state there is currently no convincing evidence that the tail bristles are homologous to the integumentary filaments of theropod dinosaurs.
A 2016 study concluded that the tail structures were highly modified scales rather than feathers due to their morphology and anatomy.
